[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Gabe, Victor –

Ahead of Thursday's board discussion, I need the gross margin figure for Q3 explained in plain terms. Specifically, the 41.2% we reported versus the 43.8% from Q2 – what drove the drop? I have my own numbers on COGS and pricing, but I want your read before I put this in front of the board.

Please send a short note (bullet points are fine) with the key drivers by Wednesday end of day. If you have a supporting schedule, attach it – I’ll pull what I need from that.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Gabe,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Your breakdown tracks with what I'm seeing on COGS and pricing — the packaging invoice timing is the one I hadn't fully isolated, so appreciate the callout. I'll pull the schedule you attached and reconcile it against my numbers before I finalize the board deck.

No need to walk through it Thursday morning unless something new surfaces; I have what I need. If you spot any other adjustments between now and then, flag them before EOD Wednesday.

Dana

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Dana,

Here's the quick read on the Q3 vs Q2 gross margin drop (41.2% vs 43.8%). Four drivers, in order of impact:

- Packaging invoice timing — roughly $180k of Q2 packaging costs hit Q3 instead, pulling margin down about 0.9 pts.
- Mix shift — Q3 had a higher share of lower-margin SKUs (the retail promo line), costing about 0.8 pts.
- Freight — spot rates on two west-coast lanes ran ~6% above Q2 average, about 0.5 pts.
- Pricing — one large account renewal at a 2% discount effective mid-quarter, about 0.4 pts.

Net effect: the 2.6 pt decline is almost entirely timing and mix, not a structural margin issue. Excluding the packaging timing, normalized margin lands around 42.1%.

I don't have a separate schedule beyond what Gabe attached — his breakdown covers the same items. If anything new surfaces before EOD Wednesday, I'll flag it.

Happy to join Thursday morning if you want backup during the discussion; otherwise you're set.

V

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Dana,

Quick follow-up since Thursday is right around the corner — happy to confirm the numbers we sent stand as-is:

- Q3 gross margin: 41.2% vs Q2 43.8%, a 2.6 pt decline.
- Drivers: packaging invoice timing (0.9 pts), mix shift (0.8 pts), freight (0.5 pts), pricing (0.4 pts).
- Normalized margin excluding packaging timing: ~42.1%.

No new adjustments have surfaced since my note. Gabe's attached schedule covers the same items, so you should be set for the board discussion.

If you want to walk through anything live Thursday morning, I'm available — just say the word.

V

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield, Victor Alade
Subject: Re: Margin clarification needed before Thursday

Hi Dana,

Quick final note before your Wednesday EOD deadline — I've re-checked the Q3 margin schedule one more time and everything stands as presented. The three drivers (pricing mix, the packaging invoice timing, and freight) fully account for the 260-basis-point drop, so no further adjustments have surfaced on my side.

I've attached the monthly close checklist for reference in case you want to see where the packaging invoice timing lands in our close process — it confirms that item was a one-off that won't recur in Q4.

You're set for Thursday. If anything unexpected comes up between now and then, I'll flag it immediately.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
